title: velaris.audit/1
description: What a Velaris program declares, names and promises, before it runs: velaris-spec SPEC.md section 8. Within version 1 fields may be added and consumers must ignore fields they do not know, so no object here forbids other properties; fields added after version 1 was first released (2.52) are optional. This schema checks shape. It does not check the rules of SPEC.md section 8 that JSON Schema cannot state - for example that effects is sorted, or that it is the union of the functions' effects.

velaris_version.description: The version of the implementation that produced the document.

ok.description: True when the program compiled: it parsed, and the checks made before running - of main, effects, types and proofs - reported no problem. When false, no other field is a bound on anything.

effects.description: The union of the declarations of every function defined in the audited file, sorted. An upper bound on the effects a run can attempt when ok is true.

functions.description: One entry per function defined in the audited file, in source order. Inline function values are not listed.

proven_share.description: Percent of the functions carrying a requires or ensures whose status is proven, to one decimal; null when no function carries one.

safe_command.description: 'velaris <file> --allow ' followed by the grant text of SPEC.md section 8.3, or by '' when that is empty. '<file>' is literal text for the reader to replace.

warnings.description: Sentences for a human reader. Their wording is not part of the format; do not parse them.

ffi_modules.description: Added in 2.60. Top-level module names given as literal text in the module argument of py, py_int, py_float, py_json and py_new, anywhere in the program as loaded. A module named by a value computed at runtime is absent, and nothing marks that one exists (SPEC.md 8.4).

loops_unshown.description: Added in 2.62. Loops in the audited file whose termination the reference's rule does not show, including loops inside inline function values.

contract_coverage.description: Added in 2.62. Functions in the audited file that take or return a List, a Map or a record and carry no requires or ensures.

fs_paths.description: Added in 3.0. Literal path arguments, as written and not resolved: read from read_file and file_exists, write from write_file, anywhere in the program as loaded. read_any and write_any say that some call's path was not a literal.

net_hosts.description: Added in 3.0. Hosts named in literal URLs given to fetch, post, fetch_status and request, anywhere in the program as loaded: the host lower-cased with trailing dots removed, or host:port when the URL writes a port. IPv6 hosts are written without brackets, which makes host:port ambiguous for them (SPEC.md 8.4). any says that some URL was not a literal or had no host.

effect_name.description: One of io, env, fs, net, clock, rand, ffi. The reference implementation accepts any identifier in a uses clause and reports it here (SPEC.md 3.2, open question Q1), so the schema accepts any identifier rather than reject documents the reference really produces.

status.description: proven: every promise proven before running (only when a prover ran). checked at runtime: has promises, not all proven. no promises: no requires or ensures. error: a problem was reported on the function's line.

loops_unshown.description: Added in 2.62. Loops in this function whose termination is not shown.
